All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Originated in the context of Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) inverse rendering, specifically for self-calibrating and fully differentiable NLOS reconstruction [S1].

The claim states that the method originated in the context of Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) inverse rendering, specifically for self-calibrating and fully differentiable NLOS reconstruction. The provided evidence from Source [S1] explicitly describes a 'Differentiable transient rendering' pipeline (Section 4.3) that computes time-resolved illumination through a forward pass involving implicit surface points and normals. It details the differentiation of the rendering process (e.g., discretization using a differentiable Gaussian distribution, avoiding binary visibility differentiation by using volumetric intensities) and optimization of system parameters (Section 4.4) to minimize loss between measured and rendered data. This confirms the method is fully differentiable and used for inverse rendering (estimating geometry and parameters from measurements). The context of NLOS is implied by the mention of 'third-bounce time-resolved light transport', 'relay wall', and paths starting at a laser ($x_l$) and ending at a sensor ($x_s$) via an intermediate surface, which are characteristic of NLOS setups. The 'self-calibrating' aspect is supported by the optimization of system parameters including laser-sensor model parameters ($Θ_{ls}$) and implicit geometry ($Θ_G$). Therefore, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
supported
